extracted.intended_audience: researchers and graduate students in political communication, media effects, and survey-based political science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, measuring, and analyzing studies of selective exposure and political media use (survey measures, variable construction, controls, panel/over-time analyses, and sensitivity checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on topic- and habit-specific selective exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain topics, such as politics, are more likely to inspire selective exposure and research should investigate habitual media exposure patterns, as opposed to single exposure decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design research to consider topic salience (politics vs nonpolitical subjects) and to measure habitual/patterned media behavior rather than one-off choices; interpret findings in light of topic-specific likelihood of selective exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure media exposure using content-based exposure rather than frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The media dependent variables measured content-based exposure (as opposed to frequency of exposure), which may be easier for respondents to accurately recall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer asking respondents what outlets/programs they access (content/outlet identification) rather than only how often they use media; content-based measures can improve recall accuracy and validity of exposure measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use open-ended questions for outlet/program recall
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, respondents were asked open-ended questions about their media exposure, so they would have to recall the name of the media program or outlet in order to answer the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask open-ended 'which outlet/program' questions to elicit specific outlet names (reduces satisficing and may improve validity); consider transcription/coding burdens and plan content analysis accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code non-consumers as zero and restrict follow-ups to consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Only those respondents indicating that they consumed each of the various types of media were asked these questions. Those indicating that they did not consume each media type were coded as 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing surveys, screen for media consumption before asking detailed exposure questions and code non-consumption consistently (e.g., 0) to avoid spurious missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine similar items when distributions are similar
rubrics_metrics.description: Two questions were combined to form this variable. The first read: how many days in the past week did you access information about the campaign for president online? The second read: how many days in the past week did you read information about the campaign for president online? Though the two had slightly different means, they had similar distributions and were combined throughout the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If related items have similar distributions and conceptual overlap, combine them to form a single measure—but report descriptive differences and justify combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct political predisposition measures carefully and run sensitivity tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The partisanship and ideology measures were combined to create a single measure of political predispositions. Analyses were run to assess whether results changed if partisanship or ideology were included separately in the models or if respondent political leanings were included in the models as a categorical variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When measures (e.g., ideology and partisanship) are highly correlated, combining may be justified; however, always run robustness/sensitivity analyses entering them separately and as categorical variables to check stability of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include demographic and substantive controls throughout analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls (see the appendix) are incorporated throughout the analysis to help to take into account differences between the population and the sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controls such as education, income, race/ethnicity, gender, age, media use frequencies, attention measures, political discussion, political interest, and strength of ideology/partisanship to reduce confounding; report control definitions and descriptive statistics (means, SDs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use panel and over-time analyses to assess causal direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Over-time analyses suggest that people’s political beliefs motivate their media use patterns and panel analyses were conducted to examine the reverse causal direction; namely, whether partisan media use contributes to ideology/partisanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible use panel data and over-time models to investigate directionality (beliefs -> media use and media use -> beliefs); report time interactions and interpret cautiously given potential confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test moderators via interaction terms (age, gender, time, ideology/partisanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses were run with the addition of an interaction between age and ideology/partisanship or an interaction between female and ideology/partisanship. Additional analysis was run adding interactions between time, ideology/partisanship, age, and gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly test moderation by demographics and time using interaction terms; report when interactions are inconsistent or non-significant and explore three-way interactions if theory suggests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and evaluate measurement reliability and coding rules for knowledge items
rubrics_metrics.description: General political knowledge battery was asked of a random two-thirds of respondents... collapsed into a dichotomous measure where scores of A and B were coded as 1 and C, D, and F were coded as 0, α = 0.64. Don’t know and refused responses were coded as incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide item-level information, decision rules for collapsing scores, internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha), and coding rules for DK/refused; assess sensitivity to different cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include attention measures for media content
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents were asked how much attention they paid to stories/articles about the campaign for president in each media type with response options: no attention at all (0), not too much, some, and a great deal of attention (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure not only exposure but attention/engagement with a simple ordinal scale and include these measures as covariates or moderators to distinguish mere exposure from engaged consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and address limitations of self-reported exposure measures
rubrics_metrics.description: There is some debate about the accuracy of survey-based media exposure measures. Two components of this study, however, may boost confidence in the measures... If, however, the media use measures employed in this study did not reflect actual media use, a link between political predispositions and media use would continue to have import: It still would mean that people recognize and report media outlets matching their political predispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss measurement error concerns for self-reports, justify chosen measures (e.g., content-based, open-ended), and explain how findings retain substantive meaning even if recall is imperfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare across media types to detect differential selective exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: This study investigates whether different media types (newspapers, political talk radio, cable news, and Internet) are more likely to inspire selective exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design analyses to compare multiple media platforms separately (print, radio, cable, online) because selective exposure processes may vary by medium; report media-specific models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct robustness and sensitivity checks (e.g., exclude variables, alternate codings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When general political knowledge was excluded, however, the interaction was no longer significant. Results are unchanged if partisanship and ideology are included separately in the analysis. Analysis also was repeated using a combination of ideology and partisanship as a categorical variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run robustness checks such as excluding potentially influential covariates, changing coding schemes, and using alternative variable specifications; report which results are sensitive to such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle item availability changes across fielding periods transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that some questions were present on the survey for only parts of this period... When these variables are employed, the analysis covers only a subset of these dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When survey items are asked only in subperiods, document this, restrict analyses appropriately, and be transparent about reduced sample sizes and potential bias from partial measurement.
